title: Statistics: Mean Deviation, Variance and Standard Deviation
seo_title: Statistics Class 11 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 13)
standard_text: Measures of dispersion; range, mean deviation, variance and standard deviation of ungrouped and grouped data (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 11 Statistics worksheet (NCERT Chapter 13): range, mean deviation about the mean and median, variance and standard deviation for raw and grouped data, and comparing consistency. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Mean deviation = Σ|x − a| ÷ n; variance = Σ(x − x̄)² ÷ n.
key_sub: Standard deviation σ is the square root of the variance.
body_html:
How it works

  • Range = largest value − smallest value.
  • Mean deviation about a (the mean or the median): Σ|x − a| ÷ n, or Σf|x − a| ÷ Σf for a frequency table.
  • Variance σ² = Σ(x − x̄)² ÷ n = Σx² ÷ n − x̄²; standard deviation σ = √(variance).
  • Adding a constant to every value does not change σ; multiplying every value by k multiplies σ by |k|.
Example

Find the mean deviation about the mean of 6, 7, 10, 12, 13, 4, 8, 12.

x̄ = 72 ÷ 8 = 9

Σ|x − 9| = 3 + 2 + 1 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 1 + 3 = 22

22 ÷ 8

Answer: 2.75

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting the absolute value in the mean deviation.
  • Giving the variance when the question asks for the standard deviation.
  • Adding a constant to σ when every value is increased.

faq.q: Which is used more, mean deviation or standard deviation?
faq.a: Standard deviation, because it works well with further calculations.
No. It is an average of squares.
